questions.statement: It is 8 p.m. Daniela sees her neighbor. What does she say?
questions.context: Son las 8 de la noche en un conjunto de Soacha y Daniela se encuentra con su vecino en el ascensor.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Good morning is for the morning, before 12 p.m., and it is 8 p.m.
Correct. Good evening is the greeting for the evening, and 8 p.m. is evening.
Incorrect. Good afternoon is for the afternoon, from 12 p.m. to about 6 p.m.
Incorrect. Thank you is to show you are grateful, not to greet a person.

questions.explanation: Para saludar de noche usamos "Good evening" (buenas noches al llegar). "Good morning" es por la mañana y "Good afternoon" por la tarde. "Thank you" es para dar las gracias.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Ana has twelve crayons. Her aunt gives her eight more. How many crayons does she have now?
questions.context: Ana tiene 12 colores en su cartuchera y su tía en Tunja le regala 8 colores más.

options.feedback: Correct. Twelve + eight = 20, and 20 is twenty.
Incorrect. Eighteen is 18, but 12 + 8 = 20.
Incorrect. Twelve is the number before her aunt gives her more; 12 + 8 = 20.
Incorrect. Four is 12 - 8; she gets more crayons, so we add, not subtract.

questions.explanation: Sumamos: 12 + 8 = 20. En inglés 20 se dice "twenty". "Eighteen" es 18 y "four" sería el resultado de restar, pero Ana recibe más colores, entonces sumamos.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: "The flag of Colombia is yellow, blue and ____."
questions.context: En el colegio de Rionegro los niños pintan la bandera de Colombia para el 20 de julio.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Green is not on the Colombian flag; it has yellow, blue and red.
Correct. The flag of Colombia has three colors: yellow, blue and red.
Incorrect. White is not a color of the Colombian flag; the third color is red.
Incorrect. Black is not on the Colombian flag; its colors are yellow, blue and red.

questions.explanation: La bandera de Colombia es amarilla, azul y roja: en inglés "yellow, blue and red". Por eso la palabra que falta es "red" (rojo).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Mateo vive en Duitama y los domingos visita a la mamá de su mamá.

options.feedback: Incorrect. An aunt is the sister of your mother or father, not her mother.
Incorrect. A sister is a girl with the same parents as you.
Correct. The mother of your mother is your grandmother.
Incorrect. A cousin is the child of your aunt or uncle.

questions.explanation: La mamá de tu mamá es tu abuela, en inglés "grandmother". "Aunt" es tía, "sister" es hermana y "cousin" es primo o prima.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "This animal is a bird. It is green and it can repeat words."
What animal is it?
questions.context: En la Amazonia, cerca de Leticia, hay muchas aves de colores que pueden repetir sonidos.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A cow is a farm animal that gives milk; it is not a bird.
Incorrect. A fish lives in water and swims; it is not a bird.
Incorrect. A monkey climbs trees, but it is not a bird and it cannot repeat words.
Correct. A parrot is a green bird that can repeat words.

questions.explanation: El loro, "parrot", es un ave ("bird") verde que puede repetir palabras ("repeat words"). La vaca, el pez y el mono no son aves.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Juan wears a cap on his head, a T-shirt and shorts."
What does Juan wear on his head?
questions.context: Juan va a jugar al parque en Girardot, donde hace mucho calor.

options.feedback: Correct. The text says "a cap on his head".
Incorrect. Shorts are for the legs, not for the head.
Incorrect. A T-shirt is for the body, not for the head.
Incorrect. Shoes are for the feet, and the text does not mention shoes.

questions.explanation: La gorra, "cap", se usa en la cabeza ("head"). La camiseta ("T-shirt") va en el cuerpo y la pantaloneta ("shorts") en las piernas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "It is sunny and very hot in Cartagena today."
What is the best thing for Maria to take to the beach?
questions.context: Maria va a la playa de Bocagrande en Cartagena un día de mucho sol.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A coat and boots are for cold weather, and it is very hot.
Incorrect. A scarf keeps your neck warm in cold weather, not in hot weather.
Correct. A hat and sunglasses protect you from the sun on a sunny day.
Incorrect. Gloves keep your hands warm, and it is a very hot day.

questions.explanation: Si está soleado y hace calor ("sunny and very hot") necesitamos protegernos del sol con sombrero ("hat") y gafas de sol ("sunglasses"). El abrigo, la bufanda y los guantes son para el frío.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Today is Friday. Ana's party is in two days."
What day is the party?
questions.context: Ana vive en Santa Marta y prepara una fiesta para el fin de semana.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Saturday is one day after Friday, but the party is in two days.
Incorrect. Monday is three days after Friday, not two.
Incorrect. Thursday is the day before Friday, and the party is in the future.
Correct. Friday + two days: Saturday is one, Sunday is two.

questions.explanation: Contamos desde el viernes ("Friday"): un día después es sábado ("Saturday") y dos días después es domingo ("Sunday"). Por eso la fiesta es el domingo.
questions.subject: ingles
